_comment: STING room numbering — corporate baseline. Override per project at <project>/_BIM_COORD/room_numbering.json; project schemes win by Id and a project DefaultSchemeId wins outright. Pattern tokens: {lvl} {dept} {seq} {seq:Dn}. Order: Serpentine | RowMajor | ColumnMajor. RowBandMm is the height of one horizontal band in millimetres — rooms whose centres share a band are one row, sorted left to right.
_warning: PreserveExistingNumbers defaults to true on every scheme here, and should stay true on anything used after a drawing issue. Renumbering a room silently invalidates every RFI, snag, O&M reference and door schedule entry that names it.

schemes.name: Level hundreds (101, 102, ... / 201, 202, ...)
schemes._comment: The North American convention. The level digit lives in startAt, which the command offsets per level, so the pattern itself carries only the sequence.

schemes.name: Department + sequence (WARD01, THEATRE01, ...)
schemes._comment: Healthcare and lab work, where a room's department matters more than its position. Department is stripped to letters and digits — Revit will not accept punctuation in a room number.

schemes.name: Level + row-major, gaps of 10 (GF010, GF020, ...)
schemes._comment: Leaves room to insert a room later without renumbering its neighbours — the reason a step of 10 is worth the wider numbers.
